items.question: How do I build a profile that feels trustworthy?
items.answer: Add a recognizable photo, a short bio, your general location, relevant skills, and a clear explanation of how you usually collaborate. A complete profile helps other people understand what you offer and improves trust across the platform.

items.question: What parts of my profile are visible to other users?
items.answer: People can usually see the information needed to assess whether collaborating with you makes sense, such as your name, image, general location, bio, skills, and public activity. Sensitive personal information should not be shared openly unless strictly necessary.

items.question: Can I change the platform language?
items.answer: Yes. The interface supports switching between Spanish and English so navigation and help content match your preference.

items.question: How can I tell whether a profile or service looks reliable?
items.answer: Review the profile completeness, service clarity, approximate location, ratings, and whether the description explains what is included. It is also a good idea to ask questions through chat before confirming an exchange.

items.question: How do I find services that are actually relevant to me?
items.answer: Use text search, category and type filters, duration filters, and nearby discovery. If location is enabled, the platform can prioritize nearby services and display them on the map for a more practical overview.

items.question: What is the difference between in-person, virtual and hybrid services?
items.answer: In-person services happen at a physical location, virtual services are fully online, and hybrid services combine both. Understanding this before requesting a service helps avoid operational misunderstandings.

items.question: How should I request a service properly?
items.answer: Open the service detail page, review the description, location and duration, and then send a request. If there are logistical details or specific expectations, include a short message to provide context from the start.

items.question: What makes a service listing feel professional and credible?
items.answer: The strongest listings clearly explain the value offered, target audience, format, duration, expected outcome, and any prerequisites. Adding an image, a clear description and a usable location also improves credibility.

items.question: Why do some services appear on the map and others do not?
items.answer: Only services with a sufficiently defined location can be shown accurately on the map. Virtual services or listings without coordinates may still appear in the list view but not in the geographic view.

items.question: What happens after I send a request?
items.answer: The request enters the exchange flow and the other user can review it, accept it, reject it, or continue the conversation before confirming. This gives both sides room to clarify expectations before committing.

items.question: How should messaging be used inside an exchange?
items.answer: Messaging should be used to clarify availability, format, scope and practical details. Keeping important agreements in writing makes the collaboration easier to manage and reduces the risk of confusion.

items.question: What do exchange statuses usually mean?
items.answer: The flow usually goes through pending, confirmed, in progress and completed. These statuses help both sides understand the current stage of the collaboration and keep the process visible.

items.question: What should I do if an exchange stops making sense or something goes wrong?
items.answer: Communicate as early as possible inside the exchange, explain the situation clearly, and avoid leaving the other person without context. Early communication usually prevents most friction.

items.question: What are communities for inside the platform?
items.answer: Communities bring together people with shared interests, goals or contexts. They help create continuity, stronger participation and more collaboration opportunities beyond one-off requests.

items.question: How do I create a useful community instead of an empty one?
items.answer: A strong community has a clear purpose, a defined audience and a description that explains what members can expect. Communities work better when they are built around real interaction, not just visibility.

items.question: Who can edit a community?
items.answer: Usually only the creator or someone with equivalent permissions can edit the community name, description, image and privacy settings.

items.question: What is the difference between a public and a private community?
items.answer: A public community is easier to discover and grow, while a private community is better for curated or sensitive participation contexts. The right choice depends on the goal of the group.

items.question: Should I share my exact address from the beginning?
items.answer: Usually no. It is better to keep the location general during discovery and only share exact logistical details when the exchange is clear or confirmed. This improves privacy and reduces unnecessary exposure.

items.question: How can I reduce misunderstandings before collaborating?
items.answer: Clarify the scope, duration, format and expected outcome before moving forward. The clearer the agreement is upfront, the smoother the collaboration tends to be.

items.question: Which signs suggest I should review a proposal more carefully before accepting?
items.answer: Ambiguous descriptions, incomplete profiles, shifting conditions or unclear communication are all signs that you should ask more questions before confirming an exchange.
